Derived public-data snapshot for "What Software Lists Tell Us About
Occupations"

Source: O*NET 30.3 Database, U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and
Training Administration (USDOL/ETA), Software Skills table.
https://www.onetcenter.org/dl_files/database/db_30_3_text.zip
License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA.

onet2r has modified this information by converting the Software Skills
table into binary occupation profiles of exact workplace examples and
calculating example and category prevalence, inverse document frequencies,
normalized binary-presence TF-IDF summaries and ranks, total-variation and
Jaccard distances between occupations, Sorensen replacement and
nestedness components for selected pairs, nearest-neighbor sets with ties
retained, neighbor-overlap sensitivities, coverage flags, multiple-route
counts, and information summaries at the workplace-example, category and
category-family grains.
Occupation titles, workplace example names and category names are retained
as source labels. Software and product names in the workplace examples may
be trademarks of their owners.
USDOL/ETA has not approved, endorsed, or tested these modifications.

Regenerate from the repository root with the current package installed:
Rscript data-raw/occupational-software.R path/to/db_30_3_text.zip

provenance.csv records the source URL, SHA-256, row and occupation counts,
and the weighting and resolution choices. The raw archive is not bundled.
No employment weighting is applied. These are descriptive tables for an
article. They are not an exposure measure, and the package exports no
substantive measure from them.
Carry this attribution/license/modification notice with separate CSV copies.
